statement.text: The process-ownership branch was recorded at the exact published revision while its terminal local release proof was still unresolved.
The process-lifecycle diagnostics work introduced typed termination outcomes and a dedicated caller-adoption guard.
The source-inventory work centralized traversal and represented scan loss as a typed inconclusive outcome instead of silently dropping subtrees.
All three harness adapters completed two hash-bound passes without source failures; marginal new evidence was three, two hundred twenty-nine, and one respectively.
Source inspection rejected at least two lexical candidates as unrelated, demonstrating that candidate retrieval alone is not evidence promotion.
Evidence, narrative, and state remain separate output planes.
The public projection contains metadata and aggregate findings, not raw conversation content.
Private identifier terms are supplied at build time and are not embedded in the package or its errors.
The second harness has not reached diminishing returns because its second pass found two hundred twenty-nine distinct records.
The content relevance of the two second-pass third-harness candidates remains unreviewed.
The terminal local release outcome was outside the frozen source window.
The third harness was not unavailable: a read-only, hash-bound snapshot supported two complete passes.
A lexical match was not sufficient for promotion: source inspection rejected unrelated candidates.
